articles.title: Predicting Gerrit Cole, Yankees Rotation and Lineups for Wild Card vs. Red Sox
articles.summary: Though nothing is set in stone yet, all signs continue to point toward the New York Yankees hosting the Boston Red Sox in the wild card round of Major League Baseball's postseason for a second consecutive year.
articles.body:
Though nothing is set in stone yet, all signs continue to point toward the New York Yankees hosting the Boston Red Sox in the wild card round of Major League Baseball's postseason for a second consecutive year.

Sure, if the Yankees sweep the four-game set at home against Tampa Bay that begins next Tuesday, they could still win the AL East and avoid playing in the wild card round at all. It's also possible (though extremely unlikely) that Boston collapses so drastically down the stretch that it ends up either as the No. 6 seed or outside the postseason picture altogether.

As of Sunday morning, though, FanDuel had the Yankees at -1100 to earn the AL's No. 4 seed, while Boston appears so locked into the AL's No. 5 seed that it's the only one of the 12 postseason spots on which FanDuel is no longer taking action.

A bracket featuring 4. NYY vs. 5. BOS is so inevitable at this point that we're ready to start projecting the roster that the Yankees will bring into that no-love-lost clash.

Before we can do that, however, how healthy are the Bronx Bombers?

2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. suffered a sprained right thumb in the middle of last week, landing on the IL on Thursday. Bryan Hoch reported that Chisholm "expects to play before the end of the regular season," hoping to return for the season-ending seven-game homestand.

CF Trent Grisham is recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring strain suffered on Sept. 4. Per Yankees beat writer Gary Phillips , manager Aaron Boone said on Sunday it's possible Grisham could return by the end of the regular season, "but he doesn't have a clear timeline yet."

DH Giancarlo Stanton is still hitting in his months-long recovery, but a return to the lineup is nowhere near imminent. He reaggravated his initial right calf injury in June and then injured the left calf when he fell running the bases in August. When the latter occurred, it rather felt like the final straw and that we won't see him again until 2027.

RHP Clarke Schmidt has made five appearances in his rehab from Tommy John surgery, nearing a return to the big leagues as a reliever. Schmidt has struck out 11 of the 26 batters he has faced and could be quite the eleventh-hour solution to the Yankees' eighth inning woes. (4.74 ERA against in the eighth compared to a sub-3.00 ERA in the fifth, sixth, seventh and ninth innings.)

LHP Ryan Weathers has been out for three weeks with a flexor strain in his throwing arm. He has been throwing long toss, though, and they hope to get him throwing off a mound in the coming days. Along with Schmidt, he, too, could factor into the bullpen mix in October.

Yankees Projected Starting Lineups vs. Boston

Provided Chisholm is healthy, the only real question is which direction the Yankees opt to go with the left half of their infield—and whether Anthony Volpe factors into the mix at all.

We can pretty well assume it'll be Goldschmidt leading off against Boston's southpaws, but definitely not starting against Sonny Gray, against whom he is 1-for-26 in his career. Garcia (4-for-10 with one HR off Gray) should be in the cleanup spot for that one and the primary pinch hitter for the other two games.

We can also pretty well assume that Judge and Bellinger will be at Nos. 2 and 3 in the order, even though Judge is just 3-for-17 with nine strikeouts and no extra-base hits since his return from the IL.

McMahon has not hit well at all against lefties this season, but he does have solid career numbers against Suarez (6-for-16 with one home run). If he only starts one game in the series, it might be that one.

Amed Rosario could be an intriguing option in either of the first two games. He is 7-for-24 (.292) in his career against Gray, as well as 5-for-15 (.333) with two home runs and no strikeouts against Suarez. Maybe Boone starts him and saves McMahon as a pinch hitter instead of the other way around.

Yankees Projected Starting Rotation vs. Boston

Indisputable. Not only is he the frontrunner for AL Cy Young and a plausible candidate for AL MVP , but he has eviscerated the Red Sox thus far in his young career. New York will be hoping for a repeat of his 8.0 IP, 0 R, 12 K masterpiece from Game 3 of last year's wild card series.

If he's physically good to go for up to 100 pitches, this one also should be relatively indisputable. Since signing with the Yankees, Fried has made six starts (including Game 1 last year) against Boston, owning the Red Sox to the tune of a 1.24 ERA and a 10.2 K/9.

Gerrit Cole is one of the highest-paid pitchers on the planet, and he hasn't missed a single turn through the rotation since making his season debut in late May.

However, he has been getting shelled as of late, allowing seven home runs over his last two starts, saddled with a 6.48 ERA (and a 7.30 FIP) thus far in September.

Even if you're inclined to disregard that recent rough patch and just ride with the 2023 Cy Young winner in a do-or-die situation, there's also this:

Gerrit Cole vs. Boston (regular seasons 2021-26) : 75.0 IP, 6.36 ERA Gerrit Cole vs. Boston (postseason career) : 8.0 IP, 7.88 ERA

Gerrit Cole vs. Not-Boston (regular seasons 2021-26) : 726.1 IP, 2.90 ERA Gerrit Cole vs. Not-Boston (postseason career) : 125.1 IP, 2.44 ERA

Schlittler and Fried have owned the Red Sox, but Boston has had Cole's number since long before his recent schneid began.

The dream scenario, of course, is that there is no Game 3 and that Cole instead toes the rubber in Game 1 of the ALDS in Tampa Bay—against whom he has made four career postseason starts with a 1.66 ERA.

If there is a Game 3, though, Rodón and his 2.25 ERA over the past month should be the way to go.

If Boone has the courage to go that route and the Yankees get eliminated without Cole ever throwing a pitch in three games, surely the responses will be calm, cool and collected, right?

articles.title: Yankees Address Legionella Bacteria Found in Stadium Cooling Tower amid Investigation for Outbreak
articles.summary: The New York Yankees said there's no connection between the cases of Legionnaires' disease in the Bronx and the bacteria that was discovered in a cooling tower at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees said there's no connection between the cases of Legionnaires' disease in the Bronx and the bacteria that was discovered in a cooling tower at Yankee Stadium.

"No current cases have been associated with Yankee Stadium," the team said, per the Associated Press . "Additionally, the New York City Department of Health has not at any point this month asked us to postpone our games."

The city's health department confirmed there have been 10 positive cases of Legionnaires' disease, with one death and three people hospitalized.

The city said Sunday health department officials tested cooling towers throughout the Bronx. Ten were flagged as testing positive for Legionella bacteria. The results didn't indicate whether the bacteria were alive or dead or whether the sites led to any exposure.

Yankee Stadium was one of the locations impacted. The Yankees told the AP they had their cooling tower drained and cleaned Sunday morning.

The Bronx Bombers wrapped up a six-game home stand later that day with a 2-0 win over the New York Mets.

The team has a pair of road series against the Minnesota Twins and Arizona Diamondbacks before returning to the Bronx on Sept. 22.

The city of New York advised residents to be diligent in the wake of the ongoing situation.

"Any New Yorkers who currently live or work in this area or people who have visited the area since late August and are experiencing flu-like symptoms, such as fever, cough, or difficulty breathing, should contact a healthcare provider immediately," the city said. "Legionnaires' disease is deadly but can be effectively treated if diagnosed early."

articles.title: Why NL exec believes Red Sox are in 'best position' to win AL championship
articles.summary: There are a few key players behind why the Red Sox can make a deep run this year.
articles.body:
The 2026 season for the Boston Red Sox has been quite a wild ride, and heading towards October and postseason baseball, things could get a whole lot stranger.

For this Red Sox squad, there's reason to believe that they can not only make the postseason and win a series or two, but actually win the American League Championship Series. But how?

ESPN's Jesse Rogers shared that one NL executive believes the Red Sox are "best positioned" to win the AL among the Wild Card teams thanks to their elite rotation and elite bullpen.

Red Sox pitching staff is reason why they're 'best positioned' to make surprise run

"I like the amount of arms the Red Sox can put out there in a playoff series," an NL executive said. "And then once you get to the back of a game, they're lights out with [Garrett] Whitlock and Chapman. I think they're best positioned to win from the wild-card teams. They'll keep the Yankees in the park when they play in the first round."

Boston's offense isn't as bad as it seemed earlier in the year, thanks to Roman Anthony 's return, Adley Rutschman 's trade, and the unexpected breakout of Mickey Gasper , among others.

But the real star of the show is their pitching staff. Just looking at the starting rotation, it's a group that has a real chance of holding teams down come the postseason.

Sonny Gray has a 2.76 ERA this season, Ranger Suarez is one of the best postseason pitchers in MLB history, Payton Tolle has been a breakout pitcher, and even Jake Bennett has had his moments. Patrick Sandoval is the fifth starter and won't be needed in October.

Looking to the bullpen, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman are a great duo, and with Erik Miller, Bryan Bello, and plenty of other options in a strong bullpen, this pitching staff has more than enough to shut teams down come October.

So, why are the Red Sox "best positioned" among the wild card teams to make a deep postseason run? Their elite pitching staff, both in the rotation and bullpen, should present a huge advantage for the team going forward.

It is time for our updated 2026 MLB Power Rankings ! The regular season may be winding down, but many postseason races are heating up. Both the American League and National League still have multiple teams competing for the final Wild Card spots. Meanwhile, multiple division races are far from decided. One team that is pulling away from the New York Yankees and the rest of the American League are the Tampa Bay Rays, who clinched a postseason spot last week .

The Rays are among the ball clubs who climbed our MLB Power Rankings this week.

The 93-57 Brewers continue to lead the way. The 90-59 Los Angeles Dodgers are still competing for the best record in baseball, but this Brewers ball club is currently the best team in the game.

LA is poised for another deep postseason run. Regardless of whether or not they surpass the Brewers for the best record, the Dodgers will enter the postseason with confidence. They are playing well and expect to reach the World Series for a third consecutive year.

The Rays are the first 90-win team in the American League this year. They hold a four-game lead over the New York Yankees for both the best record in the AL and the AL East standings. Superstar Junior Caminero and this Tampa Bay ball club have a clear path to reaching the World Series in 2026.

The Braves are just 5-5 over their past 10 games. Nevertheless, Atlanta holds a five-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies in the NL East.

As mentioned, the Yankees are trailing the Rays in the AL East. New York has the second best record in the AL and the ball club leads the AL Wild Card race.

The Cubs and Phillies are tied for the NL Wild Card lead. For now, Chicago remains ahead of Philadelphia in our MLB Power Rankings, but things could look different next week.

This Phillies ball club is chasing the Braves for the NL East lead. They are poised to reach the postseason as an NL Wild Card team at the very least.

Boston holds the No. 2 spot in the AL Wild Card race. The Red Sox are hoping to get a number of players back from injury ahead of the postseason. They could be a sneaky team to watch in the playoffs.

The Padres and Arizona Diamondbacks have been going back and forth for the final NL Wild Card spot for weeks, but San Diego is beginning to pull away. The Padres are currently 2.5 games ahead of the Diamondbacks for the position. There is still work to do, but San Diego is in a good position. A seven-game winning streak has helped the Padres over the past week.

The Diamondbacks have dropped two consecutive contests while the Padres are continuing their aforementioned winning streak. Arizona still has time to get back on track, but the ball club needs to begin winning consistently while hoping that San Diego's winning streak comes to an end sooner rather than later.

The White Sox's lead over the Cleveland Guardians for first place in the AL Central is suddenly only a half-game. Cleveland happens to be hosting Chicago for a three-game series beginning on Monday. This series could go a long way toward determining the winner of the division.

The Guardians are 6-4 over their past 10 games and are close to surpassing the White Sox in the AL Central as mentioned. They need to get the job done at home this week in their three-game series against the White Sox.

The Astros' lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West is just one game. Houston has dropped three consecutive contests, so this team needs to turn things around as soon as possible.

The Blue Jays remain only one game back in the AL Wild Card race. Toronto has won two consecutive games and will look to keep the momentum trending in the right direction this week.

The Pirates are climbing the MLB Power Rankings. The problem is that they play in the competitive National League. Pittsburgh is 6.5 games back of an NL Wild Card spot at the moment.

The Marlins have not had the best past couple of weeks, but this team continues to remain around the .500 mark. Miami has displayed potential despite its overall mediocre campaign.

The Cardinals are also hovering around the .500 mark. They will look to finish the 2026 season strong.

Texas is only one game behind Houston for the lead in the AL West. The Rangers have been close to surpassing the Astros for a while, but accomplishing the feat has been difficult for the ball club.

The Orioles are still technically in contention, but they are four games back of the final AL Wild Card spot. Baltimore is just 3-7 over its past 10 contests.

Elly De La Cruz has emerged as an NL MVP candidate. While he won't win the award given the presences of Pete Crow-Armstrong and Shohei Ohtani , De La Cruz's performance has been a bright spot in what has been an otherwise disappointing season for the Reds.

The Twins continue to fall out of contention. It was recently revealed that Byron Buxton will undergo hip surgery. He is hoping to be ready for 2027 spring training, which is encouraging.

The Nationals' strong offense hasn't been enough to keep them in contention this year. They are a few good pitchers away from becoming a contender, though.

It seems like I write the same thing in almost every MLB Power Rankings about the Mariners. They entered the season with lofty expectations but have been one of the biggest disappointments in the game. Nothing has changed for the 70-80 Mariners this week.

The Tigers have won four consecutive contests. They are not a contender at this point, but Detroit can still finish the season strong.

The Mets have played respectable baseball in recent weeks despite their overall underwhelming season. They are 7-3 over their past 10 games.

The Royals have failed to meet expectations in 2026. With that being said, their young core of players suggests they could compete as soon as next year.

The Giants need to figure out their franchise direction. Rebuilding may be their best decision.

The Athletics are similar to the Royals. They expected to play better this year but still feature a quality young core of players. The A's are another team that could compete next season.

The Angels, meanwhile, are similar to the Giants. They need to enter a rebuild, which, to their credit, they began at this year's MLB trade deadline. For now, they remain near the bottom of our MLB Power Rankings.

The Rockies are another team that simply needs to figure out a franchise direction. There isn't much reason to believe they will compete anytime soon despite their year of rebuilding.

articles.title: Everything Pete Alonso Said on Return to Mets' Citi Field, Fans Show Support After Orioles Contract
articles.summary: For the first time since signing with the Baltimore Orioles in December, Pete Alonso will return to Citi Field to take on the New York Mets.
articles.body:
For the first time since signing with the Baltimore Orioles in December, Pete Alonso will return to Citi Field to take on the New York Mets.

Ahead of the matchup against his former team on Monday, Alonso discussed being back in the stadium he once called home. He also talked to Mets owner Steve Cohen and had plenty of support from fans.

"New York is always going to feel like some sort of homecoming," he said. "The city is really special."

The Mets drafted Alonso in the 2016 MLB Draft, and he made his major league debut with New York in 2019. He was the cornerstone of the franchise for more than half a decade, earning five All-Star nods, NL Rookie of the Year and All-MLB First Team honors in 2019.

After seven seasons with the Mets, Alonso signed a five-year, $155 million deal with the Orioles in December to end his tenure in New York.

The Mets reportedly never made Alonso an offer because the bids he was getting from other teams were far above what New York was willing to pay to keep its star first baseman around.

Alonso said he has no hard feelings against his organization after the Mets chose not to pursue him in free agency.

"When you have something really, really good in front of you, for me especially, when it comes down to business negotiatons, you don't want to, I guess, kind of look elsewhere," Alonso told reporters. "For me, when Baltimore came, they obviously expressed some serious interest and for me, if they're expressing themselves seriously, then I'm going to listen seriously. I feel like Baltimore's home. I feel so at home and really just so genuinely happy where it's like, I really see myself in a really good way with this organization. Hopefully, I get to finish my career here as an Oriole. I'm beyond blessed to be an Oriole."

Alonso has put together a strong first season with the Orioles, recording 35 homers and 100 RBI while slashing .269/.363/.499. Just like the Mets, though, Baltimore is unlikely to reach the postseason as it sits at the bottom of the AL East at 72-78.

Alonso seemingly doesn't have any resentment against his former team, but he'll still be looking for a series win against the Mets this week.

The Giants lacked depth in the bullpen, dealt with a series of injuries which contorted lineups, and key players just looked like a shell of themselves through large parts of the season. Vitello has been ejected from multiple games this season. Frustration has settled in San Francisco like fog covering the Golden Gate Bridge.

It's since seemed like a salvageable season after seeing younger prospects such as Bryce Eldridge see the field more. articles.title: Ohtani, Skubal, Dodgers Clinch 2026 MLB Playoff Berth, Updated Bracket Picture and Standings
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading to the playoffs for the 14th consecutive season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are heading to the playoffs for the 14th consecutive season.

Los Angeles clinched its postseason berth on Monday with a 4-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds.

MLB playoff picture after two more teams clinch

Here is a look at the standings after Los Angeles clinched:

The 14 consecutive playoff appearances for the Dodgers ties the Atlanta Braves from 1991 to 2005 for the longest streak in MLB history.

Even though the Dodgers are cruising toward another NL West title, it has felt at times like the journey to get there has been a lot bumpier than in past years.

Their two big free-agent signings last offseason were Kyle Tucker and Edwin Díaz. Both players are in the midst of the worst season of their respective careers. Will Smith is also having his worst offensive season.

Shohei Ohtani is still having an elite offensive year, but it's the worst year he has had since signing with the Dodgers. Injuries have also kept him from pitching since July 3.

Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow and Roki Sasaki all missed time due to injuries. Despite all of these issues piling up throughout the year, the Dodgers still own a commanding division lead.

They also supplemented their roster during the season, most notably on Aug. 2 when they acquired Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers to shore up a pitching staff that was already loaded going into October after Snell and Glasnow returned.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto followed up his 2025 World Series MVP performance by putting together a Cy Young-caliber season in 2026. Freddie Freeman and Max Muncy remain their usual strong, steady selves in the heart of the lineup.

The Dodgers are going to enter the playoffs heavily favored to win the World Series for the third consecutive year. No team has pulled off a three-peat since the New York Yankees from 1998 to 2000.

The 2026 MLB playoffs begin with the wild card round on Sept. 29, followed by the division series starting Oct. 3.

articles.title: Aaron Judge, Yankees Clinch 2026 MLB Playoff Berth, Updated Bracket Picture and Standings
articles.summary: Despite being without star slugger Aaron Judge for over three months, the New York Yankees are back in the playoffs for the third straight year.
articles.body:
Despite being without star slugger Aaron Judge for over three months, the New York Yankees are back in the playoffs for the third straight year.

Following the Toronto Blue Jays' loss to the Detroit Tigers, the Yankees clinched a postseason berth as they seek their first World Series title since 2009. New York also beat the Minnesota Twins on Monday.

As the Yankees clinched on Monday, the New York Mets were eliminated from playoff contention.

Here's a look at the updated playoff picture and standings after New York punched its ticket to the playoffs.

The Yankees were 36-23 when Judge went down with a stress fracture in his rib at the end of May. The captain finally returned to the lineup on Sept. 8 against the Colorado Rockies, giving New York some much-needed firepower for the stretch run of the season.

During the three-time AL MVP's absence, the Yankees stayed afloat by going 45-39 over the next three months. While multiple hitters posted below-league-average numbers, a few bright spots saved New York's season.

Third-year slugger Ben Rice has enjoyed a breakout campaign, ranking seventh in the majors with 38 home runs. Trade deadline acquisition Luis Garcia Jr. added even more power to the lineup. Rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. showed the makings of a future superstar when he was called up to the majors in early August.

However, it's been the Yankees' pitching that kept them competitive throughout the year. New York leads MLB with a collective 3.24 ERA, with AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler leading a strong staff that also includes Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon.

Still, the Yankees will need some steady production from their hitters if they hope to avoid continued postseason disappointment. New York made its first World Series appearance since 2009 two years ago, only to lose to the Los Angeles Dodgers in five games. Last season, the team fell to the Toronto Blue Jays in the ALDS.

If Judge can return to his MVP form while New York's pitching staff remains dominant, the Yankees will have a strong chance to return to the Fall Classic and right the wrongs of the past few years.

articles.title: With Tarik Skubal trending up and Edwin Díaz trending down, the Dodgers are headed to the postseason yet again
articles.summary: Skubal's best start yet as a Dodger provided a strong reminder that, despite more bullpen issues, Los Angeles remains the team to beat in the National League...
articles.body:
CINCINNATI — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts is not one to beat around the bush.

Most MLB skippers, when asked an incisive question in a pregame scrum, volley back an evasive answer. Such is the job. These conduits between club and public are incentivized to deflect, obscure, shield. Uncomfortable truths are better left unshared — or, at the very least, danced around. It's better to be cliché than inflammatory. Protecting the players and their egos is paramount. This dynamic can be even more apparent in the larger markets, where one misstep can spark a torrent of headlines.

But Roberts, with three rings and more than 1,000 wins on his managerial ledger, utilizes a different approach. He is honest to a fault and beyond it.

On Monday, Roberts settled into the visiting dugout at Great American Ballpark and trained his flamethrower of forthrightness on the Dodgers' beleaguered $69 million closer, Edwin Díaz .

"He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good," Roberts replied when asked about Díaz's two-out, five-run outing in Triple-A on Sunday.

Asked if there's a scenario in which the woebegone closer, who owns a 11.85 ERA in just 16 big-league appearances this season, doesn't make the postseason roster, Roberts was unequivocal.

"Yeah. We have to go with our best pitchers. ... My bet is that he will be, but you know, again, there's gotta be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. My bet is yes, but we still got to see something."

Then, less than an hour before first pitch, came more bad news regarding Los Angeles ' bullpen. Edgardo Henriquez , the club's most effective relief option over the past few months, was placed on the IL due to low back discomfort. He's set to miss the remainder of the regular season. Imaging should reveal whether a postseason return is possible. Either way, Henriquez's absence represents yet another blow to a Dodger 'pen that has been middle-of-the-pack for most of the year.

But those late-game pitching concerns will carry much, much less weight if Tarik Skubal keeps pitching like he did on Monday.

Los Angeles' star trade-deadline acquisition delivered his best start yet in this lighter shade of blue, striking out nine Reds while not allowing a single run. He needed just 90 pitches across seven innings to produce his first scoreless showing as a Dodger. Throughout the night, Skubal leaned heavily on his four-seamer, running his highest usage on the pitch since September 2024.

After the game, Skubal admitted that perhaps he'd been overthinking things a bit as he acclimated to his new world.

"A lot of the struggle has kind of been me versus me," the left-handed hoss explained to a sizable gaggle of media. "Thinking too much out there. Not competing the way I want to compete. Thinking too much about pitch selection. Trying to be too fine at times and not challenging guys."

A simpler, heat-forward approach proved productive against the Reds. And Skubal, after a whirlwind summer of upheaval, finally seems to be settling into the new digs. Hours before his start, the two-time Cy Young winner strolled through the GABP visitors clubhouse mouthing along to Fetty Wap's "Trap Queen" as the ditty bounced from the locker room speakers.

Later, he complimented the support and game-planning staff for bringing him along. He also shared that he shook off catcher Will Smith just once against the Reds, a sign of trust within the battery.

Perhaps most importantly, Skubal's evening offered a worthwhile reminder that the Dodgers' best solution for their bullpen problems likely lies in their otherworldly rotation.

This L.A. bullpen is no worse off than it was a year ago, when three of the club's five most used relievers in the postseason — Roki Sasaki , Emmet Sheehan and Tyler Glasnow — were starters during the regular season. The strategy worked, if just barely, and there's every reason to expect the Dodgers to deploy it again, considering that their 2026 rotation is definitively better.

Barring an 11th-hour injury, these Dodgers will wield a comically imposing October rotation of Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto , Blake Snell and Glasnow. That quartet should hoover up its fair share of innings, putting less strain on what looks to be a makeshift, though potentially effective, bullpen.

Sasaki, currently on the IL but expected to return soon, and All-Star Justin Wrobleski will take up residence in the bullpen once September ends. Most likely, so too will Sheehan, who contributed massively important relief innings a year ago. They'll be joined by relief stalwarts such as Alex Vesia , Evan Phillips and Blake Treinen . The ninth likely belongs to Tanner Scott , who, after a disastrous, Díaz-like first Dodgers season in 2025, has recovered to the tune of a 2.91 ERA in 64 games.

It's not lockdown. It's not Plan A. But it's a talented group capable of weathering the storm in a Díaz-less world. That's how things played out Monday after Skubal departed the ballgame. Vesia tossed a scoreless eighth. Phillips allowed a Kentucky-bound, 457-foot solo shot to Elly De La Cruz but emerged from the ninth otherwise unscathed. Los Angeles took the 4-1 win , one that secured the Dodgers a playoff berth for the 14th consecutive season .

That's a remarkable run, one worthy of acknowledgement. So after the victory, Roberts toasted the team in a tasteful, understated ceremony. There were no suds, no goggles, no drunken rowdiness. Just a few plastic champagne glasses and some honest words of encouragement from an honest man with high standards.

"The message was, you know, we've accomplished a lot to this point," Roberts said. "All the while, not playing our best baseball."

articles.title: Yankees news: Cam Schlittler sounds off on playoff-bound NY after beating Twins
articles.summary: With their 8-3 win over the Minnesota Twins on Monday courtesy of a six-run eighth inning, the New York Yankees have booked their place in the 2026 MLB posts...
articles.body:
With their 8-3 win over the Minnesota Twins on Monday courtesy of a six-run eighth inning, the New York Yankees have booked their place in the 2026 MLB postseason for the ninth time in 10 seasons. In fact, the Yankees are in the middle of a 34-year winning season streak, and during that span, they've only missed the postseason seven times.

Nonetheless, the Yankees know that making it to the postseason is only one step towards their ultimate goal of winning a World Series title. The proud franchise has won 27 World Series titles in its illustrious history, but they have not broken through since 2009.

At the very least, clinching a postseason spot gives them another chance to, perhaps, break their title drought that is already lengthy by the franchise's lofty standards. For Yankees star Cam Schlittler , he is looking forward to performing under the bright lights of the postseason.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Obviously job's not done," Schlittler told Meredith Marakovits of YES Network. "It's a great feeling. Playoff baseball is special. Being able to experience that a little bit last year is a great feeling. Taking the experience out there from last year into this season, I'm very comfortable going out there and trying to help this team win games."

The Yankees, following this latest victory, are sitting just 3.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East standings. They still have everything to play for with 12 games remaining in the regular season; after all, winning the AL East crown should guarantee that New York earns a bye into the ALDS — avoiding the dreaded Wild Card round altogether.

For Schlittler, he believes that the Yankees can indeed finish the season above the Rays in the standings.

"I think we've played them very well this year. We still got a shot to win the division. We just got to stay on this, take the momentum into the next few days and into Arizona ," Schlittler added.

articles.title: Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong Sets All-Time MLB Record
articles.summary: Pete Crow-Armstrong can’t be stopped. If you thought that the Chicago Cubs‘ superstar centerfielder might slow down at some point, you thought wrong. Take Mo...
articles.body:
If you thought that the Chicago Cubs ' superstar centerfielder might slow down at some point, you thought wrong.

Take Monday night's 7-3 Cubs win over the Braves, for example.

PCA went 4-for-5 with four RBI, a run, a double, a home run and a steal.

The homer was a two-run shot in the sixth inning, and Crow-Armstrong raised his season batting average to .281 and OPS to .945.

In the process, he set an all-time MLB record.

Crow-Armstrong now stands alone in one particular statistical combination with the most-ever in a single season.

The criteria: four-plus hits, multiple extra-base hits, and a home run.

No player in the modern era has ever had that many before, via OptaStats:

It really is a cool record, because it's almost like nesting dolls.

The hope begins with four hits — a four-hit game is an awesome MLB accomplishment.

It gets more impressive with the extra-base hits, and having multiple in the same game makes a hitter quite dangerours.

And then there's the home run ball, never easy, but exactly what it takes to land on this criteria list.

There's no question at this point that Crow-Armstrong has what it takes to break records and be a superstar.

There will just be plenty wondering whether he can achieve one final milestone.

It doesn't happen much, but a season with 40 home runs and 40 steals would still be a massively impressive accomplishment for a young player like Crow-Armstrong.

On Monday, Crow-Armstrong's home run marked his 42nd of the season. So on the 40-40 quest, PCA is already done with half.

He also has 37 stolen bases after swiping second on Monday night.

It'd be a surprise to not see Crow-Armstrong get those final three steals to complete the feat.

There have been very few 40-40 seasons in MLB history. Even as a lot of numbers and moments have gained great notoriety, there's just not been a lot of guys capable from an all-around standpoint to reach these heights.

Crow-Armstrong, though, is quite capable — and that's not to mention his overwhelmingly special centerfield defense.

Any Cubs fan looking for a jersey to wear for the next decade should find a Crow-Armstrong one that fits. He isn't going anywhere.

It's fun to speculate just how high up the ladder he can go on the potential 40-40 scale, but don't lose the fun of this.

Crow-Armstrong is trying to make very rare MLB history, and it's worth appreciating every single moment along the way — especially because even at each step, PCA often seems to be making some more history.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Best Yankees Trades in MLB's Modern Era
articles.summary: For the 34th time in 34 seasons, the New York Yankees will close out 2026 with a winning record. Any team that can do this must be good at doing business.
articles.body:
For the 34th time in 34 seasons, the New York Yankees will close out 2026 with a winning record. Any team that can do this must be good at doing business.

So, come along with us as we look back at the 10 best trades the Yankees have made in their modern era.

Though the streak of winning seasons started in 1993, we pushed the start line back to 1990 for the sake of including one trade in particular. Overall, the idea was to look for deals that have had a lasting impact on the Yankees, regardless of whether they "won" the deal in a traditional sense.

After beginning with some honorable mentions, we'll count down from No. 10 to No. 1.

Date: November 18, 1997 The Trade: New York Yankees get 3B Scott Brosius (as PTBNL); Oakland Athletics get LHP Kenny Rogers, cash

Brosius came out of nowhere in 1998 to become an All-Star and the eventual World Series MVP, so this trade gets major nostalgia points just on that account. It was mostly downhill from there, but he'll always have that epic tying home run in Game 5 of the 2001 World Series.

Date: June 29, 2000 The Trade: New York Yankees get OF David Justice; Cleveland Indians get RHP Jake Westbrook, OF Ricky Ledee, RHP Zach Day

This was the year in which Justice shrugged off an apparent decline to slam 41 home runs, including 20 in 78 games as a Yankee. He was also the ALCS MVP in 2000, largely by way of a go-ahead home run in the decisive sixth game.

Date: December 7, 2023 The Trade: New York Yankees get LF Juan Soto, CF Trent Grisham; San Diego Padres get RHP Michael King, C Kyle Higashioka, RHP Jhony Brito, RHP Randy Vásquez, RHP Drew Thorpe

Soto was only a Yankee for one season, and his decision to accept a $765 million contract with the Mets has made him a heel for many Yankees fans. Even so, his 2024 season is arguably the best of a future Hall of Fame career, and he literally put the Yankees in their first World Series in 15 years with his homer in ALCS Game 5.

The Trade: New York Yankees get SS Didi Gregorius; Arizona Diamondbacks get LHP Robbie Ray, INF Domingo Leyba; Detroit Tigers get RHP Shane Greene

Since this was 12 years ago, here's a little reminder about who Gregorius was meant to replace at shortstop when he arrived in New York: Derek Jeter.

A tall order if there ever was one, and the jury was out on whether Gregorius would ever live up to his former billing as a top prospect. His first three seasons in the bigs had yielded an 88 OPS+ and just 2.8 rWAR in 191 games.

Five seasons later, Gregorius had averaged a 102 OPS+ and 3.0 rWAR as a Yankee before departing as a free agent.

That's more of a "good" shortstop than a great one, but the experience did prove that the Yankees were onto something when they tabbed Gregorius as Jeter's heir. We'd also be remiss if we didn't mention the 2017 playoffs, when he homered three times and had an .845 OPS in the Yankees' run to Game 7 of the ALCS.

Through Gregorius played his last major league game in 2022, he didn't officially retire from baseball until this past March.

The Trade: New York Yankees get CF Curtis Granderson; Arizona Diamondbacks get RHP Ian Kennedy, RHP Edwin Jackson; Detroit Tigers get RHP Max Scherzer, CF Austin Jackson, LHP Phil Coke, LHP Daniel Schlereth

The Yankees didn't get the best end of this trade. It was in Detroit that Scherzer blossomed as a future Hall of Famer, and Jackson was a 5-WAR center fielder for a couple years there.

The Yankees nonetheless had the right idea when they acquired the "Grandy Man." He had a classic Yankee Stadium swing from the left side of the plate, which always had the potential to unlock more power.

Which is exactly what happened. Granderson clubbed 108 home runs between 2010 and 2012, the fourth-most of any hitter in the league after José Bautista, Miguel Cabrera and Albert Pujols.

This was the beginning of a stretch of years in which the Yankees' playoff returns diminished following the 2009 World Series, but Granderson did his part to keep the flame lit. Specifically in 2010 and 2011, he had a 1.042 OPS in 14 total playoff games.

His last season with the Yankees was in 2013, when injuries limited him to 61 games and just seven home runs. Yet even though he ended up leaving for the Mets and throwing shade at Yankees fans, he should be (and seemingly is) fondly remembered in the Bronx.

MLB playoff picture after two more teams clinch

The Trade: New York Yankees get SS Gleyber Torres, RHP Adam Warren, OF Billy McKinney, OF Rashad Crawford; Chicago Cubs get LHP Aroldis Chapman

It must have hurt the Yankees to watch Chapman go on to win the World Series with the Cubs, but it was ultimately no harm, no foul. The Yankees re-signed him as a free agent that winter.

Rather, he landed like a meteor with the work he did at shortstop in 2018 and in 2019. He slammed 62 home runs across those two seasons, the most all-time for a middle infielder in the first two years of his big league career. Torres was also a driving force for the Yankees in the 2019 playoffs, hitting .324 with three home runs and 10 RBI in the run-up to Game 7 of the ALCS.

It's unfortunate that the rest of Torres' Yankees career never lived up to those first two seasons, specifically in the power department. He hit just 76 long balls in his last five years with the Yankees, just 14 more than in his first two alone.

Even so, Torres was ultimately one of the better infielders in the American League between 2018 and 2024, with 15.9 rWAR that ranked 17th among his peers.

The Trade: New York Yankees get RF Nick Swisher, RHP Kanekoa Texeira; Chicago White Sox get INF Wilson Betemit, RHP Jeff Marquez, RHP Jhonny Núñez

The 2008-09 offseason was the one in which the Yankees dominated free agency, spending hundreds of millions of dollars on CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira and A.J. Burnett.

The Swisher trade, by contrast, kind of snuck in through the back door. After a successful run with the Oakland A's, he was coming off a down year with the Chicago White Sox at the precise moment when he should have been in his prime.

"We did our due diligence and we're hoping '06 and '07 are more representative of Nick Swisher," Yankees GM Brian Cashman said at the time . "That was a risk we were willing to take on."

Cashman was right. Swisher hit 105 home runs in four seasons as a Yankee, with a sturdy 124 OPS+ to boot. Some Yankees fans might remember that he tended to go cold in the playoffs, but let's do him the solid of remembering his homer in Game 3 of the 2009 World Series, which was ultimately a winning cause.

Swisher should also be fondly remembered for bringing an element of fun to the Yankees that felt alien, yet welcome. Even now, it feels amazing that they ever let someone with that much personality wear pinstripes.

The Trade: New York Yankees get RF Giancarlo Stanton; Miami Marlins get SS Starlin Castro, INF José Devers, RHP Jorge Guzmán

Consider this proof that a trade can be both a disappointment and an unequivocal win.

True, the Yankees acquired Stanton (and the remainder of his $325 million contract) when he was fresh off winning the NL MVP after a 59-homer season. And true, they have never gotten anything like that from him. His best season as a Yankee saw him post 4.4 rWAR in 2018, with injuries otherwise limiting him to an average of 76 games per season since then.

Among Yankees, though, only Aaron Judge (329) has hit more home runs than Stanton (189) since 2018. Stanton has also owned October in this span, clubbing 18 playoff homers to Judge's 13.

Still another point in Stanton's favor is that he absolutely tortured the Boston Red Sox in his early days with the Yankees. Between 2018 and 2022, he posted a .931 OPS with 14 home runs and 43 RBI in 55 games against Boston.

On top of all this, the Stanton trade never amounted to more than salary relief for Miami. The Marlins have gotten a total of 2.4 rWAR from the deal, and nobody involved has played for them since 2024.

The Trade: New York Yankees get RHP David Cone; Toronto Blue Jays get RHP Marty Janzen, RHP Mike Gordon, RHP Jason Jarvis

Let's get one thing straight about the inclusion of the Cone trade in this discussion: it wasn't necessarily assured to start a long-term partnership.

Cone was a pending free agent when the Yankees got him in 1995, and he ended up re-signing as a free agent not once, not twice, but thrice . That's how a half-year rental trade turned into six years in pinstripes for Cone.

Yet even if this valuable context, it's missing the forest for the trees. What matters is that Cone was instrumental in the Yankees' return to glory in the 1990s, and not just because he was one of the best pitchers in the league (i.e., 18.6 rWAR, 142 ERA+) between 1996 and 1999.

He further enhanced his icon status by pitching a perfect game in 1999 and by working as a steady hand with the Yankees' World Series winners in 1996, 1998, 1999 and 2000. All told, they won eight of the 12 games he appeared in.

After his initial retirement in 2001, Cone first worked as a YES Network analyst in 2002 and has been with the broadcast crew consistently since 2011.

The Trade: New York Yankees get 1B Tino Martinez, RHP Jeff Nelson, RHP Jim Mecir; Seattle Mariners get LHP Sterling Hitchcock, 3B Russ Davis

That 1995 season was the one in which Don Mattingly had finally had enough after 14 years without a World Series ring. Once he retired, the Yankees needed a new first baseman.

Enter Martinez, who was fresh off helping the Seattle Mariners deny Mattingly and the Yankees in the 1995 ALDS. That year had established the lefty swinger as a capable slugger, as he had cranked 31 home runs in only 141 games.

That was pretty much the same Martinez that the Yankees ended up enjoying through the 2001 season. He hit 175 home runs in six seasons, with a peak of 44 in a 1997 season that saw him finish second in the AL MVP voting.

Nothing wrong with that. Nothing wrong with four World Series titles either. Even if Martinez wasn't the most consistent October contributor, he did have that game-tying homer in Game 4 of the 2001 World Series.

Don't worry, Jeff Nelson. We haven't forgotten about you. As he also won four rings as a key setup man for Mariano Rivera, how could anyone ever do so?

The Trade: New York Yankees get RHP Roger Clemens; Toronto Blue Jays get LHP David Wells, LHP Graeme Lloyd, INF Homer Bush

The Yankees had to give up a very good pitcher to do this deal. Wells finished third in the AL Cy Young Award voting in 1998, and would do so again in 2000.

Even at the time, though, the mood in New York was one of giddiness. The Yankees had tried to sign Clemens in 1996, when he was merely a three-time Cy Young Award winner. By the time they got him, he'd added two more to his collection.

If anyone wants to get technical, it was only courtesy of a contract extension that Clemens eventually won his sixth Cy Young Award in 2001. He also had to re-sign as a free agent to come back for the 2003 season.

All the same, he posted 19.7 rWAR across those five initial seasons in New York, all while averaging over 200 innings per season. The Yankees also won 11 of his 17 playoff starts, highlighted by a 15-strikeout one-hitter in 2000 that has the highest Game Score of any postseason start in history.

For Clemens, specifically, it might have been his first two seasons with the Yankees alone that made it all worth it. Before those, he had zero World Series rings. After those, he had two.

The Trade: New York Yankees get RF Paul O'Neill, 1B Joe De Berry; Cincinnati Reds get OF Roberto Kelly

When the Yankees acquired O'Neill in 1992, he was already an All-Star and a World Series champion. More than that, he was a sure thing in a way that Kelly was not.

"We were looking for left-handed bats because I didn't think we had enough," said then-Yankees GM Gene Michael, who also added that trading the younger Kelly was "gambling."

O'Neill had his best years as a Yankee, notably making four All-Star teams and winning the AL batting title with a .359 average in the strike-shortened 1994 season. Of course, he also added four more World Series rings to his collection.

O'Neill had his No. 21 retired by the Yankees in 2022, and is currently in his 24th season as an analyst for the YES Network. It's not easy to become a Yankees institution, but the former Red has done so.

The Trade: New York Yankees get SS Alex Rodriguez; Texas Rangers get 2B Alfonso Soriano, PTBNL (INF Joaquin Arias)

The legacy of this trade is… complicated, to say the least. Rodriguez spent 12 years with the Yankees, a he was some kind of lightning rod for seemingly all 4,380 days.

The Yankees ultimately saved $40 million on the $275 million contract that Rodriguez signed upon opting out and becoming a free agent in 2007, due to his his second PED-related controversy . The chilly relationship with Derek Jeter was weird, too, and we probably shouldn't get into the tabloid stuff.

And yet, A-Rod is seventh on the Yankees' all-time home run list and 10th among their all-time hitters in rWAR. Without him, they also don't win the World Series in 2009, in which case they'd currently be on a 25-year championship drought.

A-Rod's peak as a Yankees was certainly between 2004 and 2007, when he won two MVPs and averaged 43 home runs and 7.7 rWAR per season. By comparison, the Rangers got a total of 3.7 rWAR out of Soriano in two seasons.

Love him? Hate him? That's up to you. What's for sure is that if Brian Cashman ever gets a chance to do this trade over again, the smart thing would be to do exactly what he did in February of 2004.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Latest 2026 MLB Playoff Bracket Predictions With 2 Weeks to Go
articles.summary: Can you refer to the playoffs this season as "October" when the first two days of the postseason slate will be on Sept. 29 and 30?
articles.body:
Can you refer to the playoffs this season as "October" when the first two days of the postseason slate will be on Sept. 29 and 30?

Whatever you refer to the postseason as, it should be a fun one.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to become the first team in a generation to win three consecutive World Series titles. However, they seem mortal as the postseason approaches, and the Atlanta Braves, Milwaukee Brewers, Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies will be among the teams vying to upset them.

Meanwhile, this is the worst American League field in more than a generation. Because of that, there's an assumption that the New York Yankees are going to get hot and return to the World Series for the second time in three years. But the Tampa Bay Rays have the best record in the AL.

As we close in on the MLB postseason, let's take a look at the latest MLB playoff bracket predictions.

Projected Wild-Card Teams: New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox

The Rays were kind of the forgotten team in this division entering the season, but Kevin Cash's squad—barring a dramatic collapse—is going to not only win the AL East, but also claim the top seed in the junior circuit.

Aaron Boone's Yankees still have an outside shot at catching the Rays, but they're most likely going to have to settle for the top wild-card spot in the AL. It's unfortunate in the sense that they have the second-best record in the AL but won't get a bye because they won't win their division. If Aaron Judge and Max Fried are healthy and productive when the postseason rolls around, they still could be the favorites to win the pennant.

Meanwhile, the Red Sox have had a miraculous in-season turnaround. At the end of June, they were 37-47. Interim manager Chad Tracy has guided them to the third-best record in the AL. They'll be in the postseason as a wild-card representative as well.

The defending AL Champion Blue Jays are worth a mention here. While we're not going to predict they get into the playoffs, they are still pushing the Cleveland Guardians for the final AL playoff spot. If Vladimir Guerrero Jr. catches fire and the Blue Jays sneak into the postseason, all we're saying is that stranger things have happened.

Projected Wild-Card Teams: Cleveland Guardians

Two seasons after losing a staggering 121 games, the White Sox are not only on pace to win the AL Central, but also to earn a first-round bye as the division leader with the second-best record.

Even if the White Sox win their division but don't get the first-round bye—or even if they have to settle for a wild-card spot—it's been a miraculous step in the right direction for this franchise. With a budding young core that includes Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, Tristan Peters, Chase Meidroth and Colson Montgomery, this should be the start of a string of successful seasons on the south side.

With that said, the Guardians are still nipping at their heels. Cleveland has a negative run differential, although they also did last season and still stole the division from the Detroit Tigers down the stretch. This year, a wild-card spot is the most likely outcome for the Guards, but the division is still very much in play.

If the Guardians can get Foster Griffin back on track, they could be a tough out in October with a rotation that also includes Parker Messick and Gavin Williams.

This division arguably doesn't even deserve one postseason representative. But between being guaranteed a division winner and the third wild-card spot, it's still possible that the AL West winds up with two playoff teams.

The Astros are the current favorites to win. When you're probably only talking about having to get to 82 or 83 wins, just having likely AL MVP Yordan Alvarez anchoring the lineup might be enough to get Houston into the postseason. However, general manager Dana Brown has already been dismissed. Even with an AL West title, manager Joe Espada might not be back in 2027.

First things first, the Astros have to get into the postseason. With the Seattle Mariners fading, the in-state rival Texas Rangers seem to be the biggest threat to the Astros. While a rotation with Jacob deGrom, Nathan Eovaldi and MacKenzie Gore could be scary in a short series, the Rangers are currently on pace to finish below .500.

The AL West best encapsulates how much of a disaster the AL is as a whole this season.

MLB playoff picture after two more teams clinch

Projected Wild-Card Teams: Philadelphia Phillies

The Braves have all but wrapped up the NL East, which will snap a two-year streak of the Phillies winning the division. Both teams will be in the playoffs, though, and there's a scenario where the Braves could host the Phillies in the NLWCS.

Ronald Acuña Jr. is red hot, which should scare the rest of the league, considering the Braves have had most of their success this season without the former NL MVP being at his best. If Acuña is going well, a Braves lineup that also includes Matt Olson, Drake Baldwin, Ozzie Albies and Michael Harris II can hit with just about anyone.

It's fair to wonder whether the Braves have enough starting pitching to make a World Series run, but Chris Sale will make them the favorites in just about any Game 1. Plus, Tyler Mahle has been tremendous since being acquired from the San Francisco Giants.

As for the Phillies, it's not hard to envision the best-case scenario where Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber are red-hot in the postseason, while the starting pitching trio of Jesús Luzardo, Zack Wheeler and Cristopher Sánchez pitch them deep into the postseason. However, this past weekend in Atlanta was troubling, particularly because Luzardo was scratched from Saturday's outing with shoulder stiffness.

Both of these teams have had similar cores for an extended period. It will be interesting to see where they go from here if one or both exit the postseason early.

The culture that the Brewers have built is about to win them their fifth division title in six seasons. However, at a certain point, it's not good enough to just be in the postseason. The Brewers have only been to the World Series once. That came when they were in the AL in 1982.

Likely NL Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski offers the clearest reason why this October could be different for the Brew Crew, who are likely to be the No. 1 seed in the senior circuit. Rookie Logan Henderson has also been excellent, though the Brewers probably don't have as many rotation options as some other NL contenders.

Pat Murphy's lineup is deeper than most fans might realize. Second baseman Brice Turang is one of the most complete players in baseball. First baseman Jake Bauers is in the midst of a career year, as he leads the NL in on-base percentage. Catcher William Contreras has an OPS above .800 since the All-Star Break. This is a lineup good enough to win a World Series.

The Cubs are still trying to lock down the top wild-card spot in the NL, but they have as good of a lineup trio as there is with presumptive NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong, Alex Bregman and Seiya Suzuki.

For the Cubs, the biggest question is whether their pitching staff can get hot and stay healthy. Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman and Shota Imanaga could be a strong group, but there are definitely health concerns (plus Gausman hasn't been great since being traded to the Cubs).

Projected Wild-Card Teams: San Diego Padres

After not having a first-round bye in 2025, the Dodgers are likely to be the No. 2 seed in the NL postseason in 2026, allowing them to surpass the wild-card round. That puts them a step closer to being the first team to win three World Series titles in a row since the Yankees did so from 1998-2000.

A year ago, the Dodgers rotation got healthy and hot at the right time. They'll need that to happen again. It appears Shohei Ohtani is done pitching this season. However, with Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow, the Dodgers should still have as good of a pitching staff as any in the postseason.

Ohtani is still hitting, and as always, a lineup including him and Freddie Freeman is going to be intimidating. What's particularly scary for the rest of the league is that Teoscar Hernández, Mookie Betts and Kyle Tucker have all heated up in September.

The Padres are currently in control of the final wild-card spot in the NL. Fernando Tatis Jr. has a .996 OPS since the All-Star Break, while Jackson Merrill is at .933. If Manny Machado heats up, this could be a tough team to face in a short series because they have arguably the best bullpen in baseball with a unit that includes Mason Miller, Adrián Morejón, Bradgley Rodriguez, Yuki Matsui and Wandy Peralta.

We can debate whether either of these teams actually belongs in the playoffs, but the Guardians have better starting pitching. It's also hard to feel great about the ability of the Astros to get the ball from their starters to closer Josh Hader with a lead intact.

For the second year in a row, the Yankees and Red Sox will meet in the ALWCS at Yankee Stadium. Last year, Cam Schlittler's coming out party was a dominant performance in Game 3. This year, the AL Cy Young contender will take the ball against his favorite childhood team in Game 1, giving the Yankees a 1-0 series lead. It may take all three games again, but we lean Yankees.

How will a team with very little collective playoff experience respond to having a first-round bye? That's fair to wonder. For the Guardians to be here, they're going to have to have gathered a little bit of momentum. That will work in their favor, as José Ramírez, Steven Kwan and the Guardians will upset the division-rival White Sox in four games.

There's an expectation that the Yankees are going to be able to flip a switch in the postseason and run through a weak AL. Perhaps they will. But Aaron Judge only just returned from a stress fracture in his right ribcage that cost him the entire summer. Max Fried has a 5.31 career postseason ERA. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is on the IL with a right thumb sprain. Itr's not a guarantee everything comes together for the Yankees in October.

Meanwhile, the Rays have been the best team in the AL wire to wire, and perhaps haven't received the respect they deserve. Well, if Junior Caminero, Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda lead the Rays to the series victory over the Yankees, no one is going to be overlooking them anymore.

Frankly, there's not one team in the AL that necessarily feels like a World Series team.

Even though the Guardians have a pitching staff that could make them dangerous in the postseason, the way they've played, they would be out of the playoff picture if they were in the NL.

The Rays don't know if they'll get Shane McClanahan back from forearm tightness. Freddy Peralta has a 4.35 ERA in seven starts since being acquired. This rotation could be tremendous at its best because Drew Rasmussen (14-5, 2.81 ERA) and Nick Martinez (14-4, 2.92 ERA) are both having excellent seasons. But it's not certain.

Still, the Rays have been the best team in the AL this season. Truthfully, the three playoff teams from the AL East are probably the best ones in the AL. Whichever of the Rays, Yankees and Red Sox goes the farthest will probably represent the AL in the World Series. The Rays are our bet.

The Braves need to get out to leads early, because with Mason Miller and the Padres bullpen looming, San Diego isn't going to blow many leads after the sixth inning. With Chris Sale looming in Game 1 and Ronald Acuña Jr. getting hot at the right time, the Braves should have enough to win this series in three games.

Part of you wonders whether Kyle Schwarber will go crazy playing a postseason series at Wrigley, and whether the Phillies will surpass the team he helped break a 108-year World Series drought a decade ago. At home, though, we'll give the Cubs the edge in three.

The best bet for the Braves will be to jump out to an early series lead, hoping that the Dodgers are groggy after the first-round bye. For as much as it might seem like the Dodgers are untouchable, they were upset by the San Diego Padres in 2022 and the Arizona Diamondbacks in 2023 under similar circumstances.

Ultimately, though, the Braves probably don't have quite enough pitching to compete with the staff the Dodgers are going to throw at them. We'll go Dodgers in four.

For as great a season as Jacob Misiorowski has had, it's fair to have some skepticism about the ability of the Brewers to translate tremendous regular-season play into a World Series run. We're not saying they can't, but the onus is on them to prove it this October.

It could get late early if the Cubs open this series by upsetting Misiorowski and company in Milwaukee in Game 1. We're going to predict that's what happens, with the Cubs ultimately knocking the Cubs out in four games.

If you're just going by talent on the roster, the Dodgers should not only win the NL pennant, but also win their third consecutive World Series. This might be the easiest path to a World Series they've had. But it is really, really hard to win two years in a row, let alone three. Call it intuition, but we think someone is going to complete the job that the Blue Jays came so close to last October.

It will take a special series from the stars, but Pete Crow-Armstrong just seems unable to miss right now. We'll predict that the Cubs upset the Dodgers in seven games, with PCA winning NLCS MVP.

This will be the third time in Rays history that they've reached the World Series. It will be the third time in as many tries that they fall short of winning the franchise's first World Series.

Remember when the Red Sox finally got through the Yankees in seven games in 2004? There were some people who thought they might have used all their energy to slay the Yankees. Instead, once they got through the boogeyman, they swept the St. Louis Cardinals.

Well, it might take the Cubs seven games to upset the Dodgers, but if they're able to prevent a three-peat, it might feel like light work to finish off the representative of a generationally weak AL.

Our prediction is that Seiya Suzuki will win the World Series MVP in a sweep, which would be quite the way to head into free agency.

articles.title: Cubs Skipper Sends Rare Dodgers Message After ‘Pretty Darn Good’ Move
articles.summary: Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell offered a surprising response about the Los Angeles Dodgers’ decision.
articles.body:
Chicago Cubs skipper Craig Counsell has established himself as a trusted dugout leader, bringing the experience of his successful Milwaukee Brewers tenure to a team that has quickly returned to National League contention.

His willingness to make creative roster decisions has become a defining part of his tenure in Chicago, though he very rarely compares one of his players to anyone else in Major League Baseball.

"Chicago Cubs manager Craig Counsell dislikes 'comps,' the baseball lingo for measuring one player against another, a shorthand form of communicating within larger evaluations," Patrick Mooney noted for The Athletic . "Counsell almost always avoids playing that game."

But with the postseason approaching, Counsell made a notable exception.

Chicago Cubs Send Los Angeles Dodgers ' Message After Key Pitcher Move

While discussing Edward Cabrera 's recent move from the Cubs' rotation into the bullpen, Counsell pointed to a Dodgers postseason success story from last year as a potential blueprint.

"A great example from last year is what Roki Sasaki did the last month, into the playoffs," Counsell said, offering a rare direct comparison with another National League player, per Mooney. "That could happen. That's a roadmap to how this could be really successful. Is that the best result? That was a pretty darn good result. But that's what you keep yourself open to."

The comparison is significant because Sasaki's transition came at an important point in Los Angeles ' season.

"The hard-throwing Dodgers righty moved into a bullpen role in September of last season and then was a key part of Los Angeles' run to the World Series title in October," Jordan Bastian reported for MLB.com . "He spun a 0.84 ERA across nine playoff appearances, including a couple multi-inning efforts. If Cabrera could follow a similar path, it would be a rousing success story for the North Siders."

Cabrera was activated from the 15-day injured list last week after dealing with another recurrence of a blister on his pitching hand. The Cubs placed right-hander Trent Thornton on the injured list with left ankle soreness to clear a spot for Cabrera and will be hoping he can have a Sasaki-like resurgence into October this season.

Chicago Cubs Land Key October Option After Pitcher Move

The bullpen experiment represents a significant change from Chicago's original plan. The Cubs acquired Cabrera from the Miami Marlins during the offseason expecting him to contribute as a starting pitcher, but injuries and blister problems repeatedly interrupted his season.

Through 15 starts, Cabrera posted a 5.68 ERA with 67 strikeouts and 32 walks over 76 innings. His move to relief gives Counsell another opportunity to maximize the right-hander's power stuff while limiting the workload that comes with starting.

The Cubs entered the final stretch of the season with postseason aspirations and a bullpen that has required additional solutions. Cabrera now represents one of the more intriguing possibilities.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani and Mamiko Tanaka’s impactful journey outside the spotlight: How their family foundation is building a lasting legacy in baseball and beyond
articles.summary: MLB News: Shohei Ohtani has spent much of his career under the brightest lights in baseball. From his historic two-way performances to his success with the Los .
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani has spent much of his career under the brightest lights in baseball. From his historic two-way performances to his success with the Los Angeles Dodgers, his name has become closely linked with greatness on the field. Yet there is another side of Ohtani that has steadily gained attention. Alongside his wife, Mamiko Tanaka, he has taken steps to make giving back part of his family’s story.The launch of the Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation created a new platform for that work. Its focus on children and animals offers a different view of the MLB superstar, one centered on community, compassion and a legacy that can last well beyond his playing career.Shohei Ohtani and Mamiko Tanaka’s family foundation supports children, youth activity and animals in needThe Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation was established with two clear areas of focus. It aims to support initiatives that encourage children to stay active and live healthier lives while also helping organizations that rescue, protect and care for animals.The foundation’s mission statement says, “Our mission is to create healthier, happier communities by funding initiatives that inspire children to stay active and live well, and by supporting programs that rescue, protect, and care for animals in need.”The organization also carries a strong family connection. Its logo features figures representing Ohtani, Mamiko Tanaka, their daughter and their dog Decoy, also known as Dekopin. That detail gives the foundation a personal touch and connects its charitable goals with the family’s own interests.For Ohtani, the foundation is not the beginning of his charitable work. Instead, it brings together causes he has already supported over the years.Animal welfare has been particularly visible in his recent efforts. After devastating wildfires struck Southern California in January 2025, Ohtani announced a $500,000 donation to help firefighters, people forced to evacuate and animals that needed assistance.His connection with animals has also reached children’s literature. Ohtani co-authored Decoy Saves Opening Day, a book inspired by his beloved dog. He said proceeds from the book would be donated to nonprofit animal rescue organizations, giving the project a purpose beyond entertainment.From 60,000 baseball gloves in Japan to disaster relief, Ohtani’s charitable work has grown with his global successOhtani’s support for children has also taken a very direct form. In 2024, he donated 60,000 baseball gloves to elementary schools across Japan. The gesture helped provide young players with equipment while connecting Ohtani’s own baseball journey with the next generation.The donation was significant because Ohtani’s rise began in Japan before he became one of Major League Baseball’s biggest stars. His success gave him a global platform, and his charitable efforts show how he has chosen to use that platform.His support has not been limited to youth baseball. The $500,000 contribution following the Southern California wildfires showed another side of his philanthropy, with his donation aimed at helping firefighters, displaced residents and animals affected by the disaster.The response from fans and supporters has also reflected interest in this quieter side of Ohtani’s life. His donations to disaster relief, support for young athletes and concern for animals have helped shape an image that goes beyond statistics and awards.The Shohei Ohtani Family Foundation now gives those efforts a long-term home. With Mamiko Tanaka and their family represented in its identity, the foundation carries a personal meaning as well as a charitable mission.Ohtani’s baseball career will ultimately be remembered through records, championships and MVP awards. But his decision to invest in children, animals and communities could give his legacy another lasting chapter. For a star accustomed to making history on the field, his family foundation offers a chance to make an impact in a very different way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mickey Mantle Photo Sells for Record $3M, Was Used for Iconic 1952 Topps Yankees Card
articles.summary: The Mickey Mantle photo that was used for the iconic 1952 Topps baseball card has been sold at auction.
articles.body:
The Mickey Mantle photo that was used for the iconic 1952 Topps baseball card has been sold at auction.

According to Darren Rovell, the picture was sold for a record $3 million at a private auction.

MLB playoff picture after two more teams clinch

Rovell noted the image has been graded as a Type 1 photo by Professional Sports Authenticator.

Per the PSA grading scale , a Type 1 photo is classified as a first "generation photograph, developed from the original negative, during the period" within approximately two years from when the picture was taken.

Type 1 photographs are described as the "most desirable and valuable of the four photograph types because of their vintage and originality."

The 1952 Topps card featuring Mantle is arguably the most valuable collectible card on the market. A 9.5-graded version was sold at auction for $12.6 million in 2022, shattering the previous record for a trading card of $7.25 million that belonged to the famous T206 Honus Wagner card.

That record has since been broken by a Michael Jordan-Kobe Bryant 2007-08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Auto that was sold for $12.9 million in 2025.

The 1952 season was Mantle's second year in the big leagues and his breakout campaign. He hit .311/.394/.530 with 23 homers in 142 games, finished third in AL MVP voting, made his first of 20 All-Star appearance and helped the Yankees defeat the Brooklyn Dodgers in the World Series.
